To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we extend the Kronecker-factored Approximate Curvature method for recurrent neural networks by introducing a novel approximate Fisher information matrix, which significantly improves the training speed and performance of recurrent neural networks on challenging training tasks.

we propose a novel approximation to compute the inverse of the FIM for recurrent neural networks, that we show that this approximation is accurate, and that we demonstrate in experiments that this approximation leads to significantly improved performance of the K-FAC optimizer on several challenging tasks for RNN training.
K-FAC is a powerful optimization technique that works well in practice, and that it is possible to extend K-FAC to RNNs in a principled manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions:
  1. A novel approximation to the curvature for RNNs that is based on a novel approximation to its Fisher information matrix.
developing and applying second-order optimization methods to the training of RNNs.
the development of novel second-order optimization methods for recurrent neural networks (RNNs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
K-FAC has a significant advantage over other optimizers for training RNNs.
the K-FAC method is an excellent choice for RNNs and that it is a good idea to use it.
our method significantly improves the state-of-the-art for RNNs, and is a promising alternative for general purpose 2nd-order methods for neural network optimization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel method for RNN training which is based on a novel approximation to 2nd order information, which is more principled than the previous method (Martens & Sutskever, 2011) which is based on the assumption that the gradient contributions at consecutive time-steps are independent, and which has been shown experimentally to give superior performance over the previous method.
we have developed a 2nd order optimization method for RNNs that is based on a novel approximation to FIM.

we propose a novel approximation to compute the Fisher information matrix for RNNs, which is based on the assumption of a chain-structured Gaussian graphical model for the statistical dependencies between the gradient contributions of the various time-steps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to design a 2nd order method for RNNs that is both effective and computationally cheap, and that the resulting algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art 1st order methods.

K-FAC can be successfully extended to a variety of network architectures by making appropriate approximations to the FIM, which is a very powerful tool for understanding the curvature of the loss landscape.
the FIM structure can be leveraged to design specialized optimizers for specific neural network architectures.
